text:
Sophie (CEO): Thanks for staying on after the all-hands. Wanted to drop the follow-up here re: the hiring phasing and a few clarifications we didn't have time for live. High-level: ~36 net-new roles spread across Eng, Product, DevEx, and Support over the next year. Details below, ask away.

Andre (People Ops): Quick timeline: hiring begins immediately. Were doing three waves: Wave 1 (Q2) ~12 hires, Wave 2 (Q3) ~14 hires, Wave 3 (Q4) ~10 hires. Internal transfer window opens today for two weeks before we go public with reqs.

Ava (Recruiter): For external candidates: the loop will be 3 stages (screen, exercise, loop). Runtime roles will include a latency/system-design exercise. Internal candidates who meet bar may get an expedited loop; reach out if you want to be flagged.

Ravi (Eng Manager): Can you break down the engineering hires by focus area?

Marta (VP Eng): Eng allocation: Runtime 7, Infra 5, Eng-ML 3, SRE/Oncall 3. Of the runtime slots, ~2 are focused on quant/low-level kernels and ~2 on caching/kv systems. Were aiming for ~40% senior/staff hires so we can move faster.

Theo (Staff SWE): If I apply to move into runtime, what happens to my current team's capacity? Also curious how promotion/comp is handled.

Andre (People Ops): Internal mobility flow: 2-week EOI period, then internal interviews over ~3-4 weeks. We try to keep comp consistent; bumps above existing bands require approval and are handled on a case-by-case basis. Managers: please coordinate backfills early.

Nina (Support Lead): How many support hires are planned? Weve been stretched supporting Dedicated customers.

Sophie (CEO): Good callout. Support/Customer Success gets 4 hires in the plan this year, with two earmarked for Dedicated onboarding and two for enterprise-level SLO/safety ops.

Liam (Product): Product hires are mostly PMs: 3 for Dedicated/enterprise features, 1 growth PM for self-serve, 1 product designer split across onboarding and docs. No core platform PMs until Q3 so we dont clog interview cycles.

Ravi (Eng Manager): Any org changes coming with new roles? Splits/merges?

Marta (VP Eng): No wholesale reorg. Expect targeted restructures: create distinct teams for "Serving Runtime" (throughput/latency) and "Serving Orchestration" (routing, autoscaling). Team diagrams will land with managers this week for feedback.

Theo (Staff SWE): Oncall concerns: runtime folks worry about burn during major rollouts. Any plans to reduce load?

Marta (VP Eng): Yes. We're introducing a resilience owner per squad, moving certain operational duties into Dedicated on-call rotations, and planning runbook and automation work. We expect peak oncall hours to drop ~15-25% after hires and runbook improvements.

Andre (People Ops): Action items: 1) publish the detailed headcount spreadsheet (EOD) 2) open internal transfer form (link in the spreadsheet) 3) schedule manager syncs to review team-level proposals.

Ava (Recruiter): For interview prep, I'll post role-specific guides and suggested reading for runtime interviews (profiling, batching strategies, quant basics).

Sophie (CEO): Thanks all. If youre worried about team changes or comp, talk to your manager or @Andre. We'll post an FAQ and a timeline doc with links in this thread. :thumbsup:
